Occupied before this task: nothing (this is the first task of the difficulty). Claimed here:
rentals_ext_damage_assessment, rentals_ext_late_handin_fee, rentals_ext_counter_settlement and
rentals_ext_security_hold_settlement, with their four tools. Reserved for task 1 (two prerequisite
problems and three computations): the reservation side of the charter — the agreement's own opening
and its rate, the shop's change of model and extension route, and the cancellation and uncollected
reservation terms. Those rest on rentals_agg_multi_holding, rentals_agg_party_pricing,
rentals_reservation_terms, rentals_swap_and_extension and rentals_cancellation, none of which this
task claims as an extended policy, and on the events rentals_reserve, rentals_confirm, rentals_swap,
rentals_extend and rentals_cancel, none of which this task writes. Task 1 therefore has an
independent, load-bearing space with a root problem and two prerequisites of its own.

DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: a guest rings because a six hundred and fifty dollar security hold from
a demo ski hire is still sitting against her card. Scored core parameter: what actually goes back to
her. The chain the policy forces between the two: what goes back is the hold standing less what is
kept back against what the agreement still owes, and the rule states that it is worked out only
after the money collected against the agreement stands against the charges raised on it. So the
agent must first get the guest to settle. What she is asked to settle is itself fixed only after
every technician's finding on the agreement carries the amount the guest bears for it, and only
after the account carries the shop fee owed for the days the kit stayed out beyond the date on the
agreement. Neither of those exists at the opening: the finding stands at nil and no fee entry of any
kind is on the account. Depth is therefore three hops (release <- settlement <- {assessment, fee});
breadth is four products read in parallel (passes, lodging, lessons, insure), three stretches of the
rental ledger (the dates the kit was out, the charge families, the hold) and one shop request
record.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST. The customer names one number, 650, and it is not the answer to anything.
Every figure that matters has to be assembled: six dates the kit was out and which serial each
carries, a waiver charged for four of those six dates, a delivery charge, an extension request the
shop never answered, eleven lift scans inside a four-month window and two more outside it, three
school sessions delivered among four school entries, a lodging departure date, a protection plan
written over this very agreement, and the running sums of five ledger families. The difficulty is
reading the policy and reconciling the ledger, never picking between similar tools: each of the four
problems has exactly one action, and the agent's whole job is to work out which problems exist and
what each one's number is.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- Write at action 12 (subject rentals_damage_charge). Governing base policy: rentals_deposit_and_damage.
  Its structured gates apply to rentals_deposit_hold and rentals_deposit_release only, so this write
  carries the policy's scope rather than a gate: what a technician finds is recorded against the
  serial of the item, not the agreement as a whole (seed: the finding entry carries item_serial
  DEMO4471KX), fair wear is not charged, and kit that never comes back is charged at the replacement
  value instead of assessed — not this case, since the agreement stands returned with a hand-in date.
  No time gate.
- Write at action 14 (subject rentals_fee_charge). Governing base policy: rentals_late_return, gate
  fee_bearing_agreement_state: "A fee is raised against an agreement only while the agreement stands
  in the confirmed, picked_up, overdue, returned, cancelled or no_show state." Authority
  system_record, pre-action; correlation key rentals_holdings.rental_id, bound to the call's
  rental_id. The agreement stands returned, which is inside the allowed set. The other gate of that
  policy, grace_has_run_out, applies to rentals_mark_overdue and is not realized by this write.
- Write at action 16 (subject rentals_payment). Governing base policy: rentals_pricing, whose only
  gate applies to rentals_rate_charge; the write carries the policy's scope, namely that the
  package's payment point decides when money is taken. Demo takes money at booking, which the seeded
  375.50 on the booking date records; the delivery charge raised later and everything raised in this
  conversation are collected afterwards, which is what the counter step does.
- Write at action 18 (subject rentals_deposit_release). Governing base policy:
  rentals_deposit_and_damage, two gates.
  hold_release_state: "A hold is released only while the agreement stands in the overdue, returned,
  cancelled or no_show state." The agreement stands returned. Positive case: returned, as here.
  Negative case: had the kit still been out and the agreement standing picked_up, the release could
  not be written at all and the correct terminal state would be to wait.
  hold_release_window (kind time): anchor event "the kit was handed in", anchor source
  rentals_holdings.returned_date = 2027-02-06, relation not_after, duration variants.
  deposit_release_days = 7 for the Demo package, unit business_days, boundary inclusive, counting
  rule copied verbatim. Counting business days forward from Saturday 2027-02-06 as day zero:
  2027-02-08 is day one, 2027-02-09 day two, 2027-02-10 day three, 2027-02-11 day four, 2027-02-12
  day five, 2027-02-15 day six, 2027-02-16 day seven. frozen_time 2027-02-09 is day two, inside.
  Just-past case: 2027-02-17 is day eight and outside. Boundary case: 2027-02-16 is day seven and,
  the boundary being inclusive, still inside.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target object: the one rental agreement on the household account, the Demo Ski
& Board Rental hired at Silverpine Basin from 2027-01-26 with a due date of 2027-01-31 and a hand-in
date of 2027-02-06. Correlation key: rentals_holdings.rental_id, which every ledger entry and the one
shop request carry. Rows that enter the sums: the three rate-family charges (315.50 hire rate, 60.00
waiver, 65.00 delivery), the payment of 375.50, the security hold of 650.00, the six dates the kit
was out and the technician's finding. Rows deliberately excluded by a visible key: the two lift scans
of 2026-03-07 and 2026-03-21, excluded from the standing share because they fall outside the
four-month window and carry season_code 2025-26; the school tuition charge, excluded from the session
count because its entry family is a tuition charge and not a session delivered; the two dates the kit
was out on serial DEMO2208RT, excluded from the inspection count because they carry the serial the
rider held before the change of model rather than the serial the agreement now shows. Settlements
already made: the payment of 375.50 carries related_event_id pointing at the hire rate entry, so it
settles the hire rate and the waiver and leaves the later delivery charge uncollected — which is
exactly the 65.00 the agreement shows outstanding at the opening. Every derived write this task makes
carries the agreement's own reference, and the assessment is written onto the very finding entry it
answers to rather than onto a fresh row.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root: rentals_ext_security_hold_settlement (release_amount_usd, agent).
  edge 1: rentals_ext_counter_settlement <- rentals_ext_damage_assessment.
    kind value_input, gate assessments_raised, form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "The amount the guest is asked to hand over is fixed only after every
    finding a technician has entered against an item on the agreement carries the amount the guest
    bears for it."
    Four-point test: (1) "only after" joins this policy's own result to what it waits on; (2) the XX
    side is a record-visible state — a finding entry on the rental account carrying an amount — and
    names no action and no performer; (3) no tool, no policy id, no snake_case token; (4) the
    strength is "only after", a hard requirement, and the scope is exactly "every finding a
    technician has entered against an item on the agreement", which is the condition the edge
    declares. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the damage assessment
    policy's own action is the only one in the charter that puts an amount on a technician's finding.
    Derivation: the sentence says the counter figure waits on findings carrying amounts; the records
    show one finding against serial DEMO4471KX standing at 0.00; the damage assessment policy's rule
    says that an item a technician has found fault with is assessed against the agreement and fixes
    what the guest bears; therefore the assessment must be written first, and it is the only reading.
    Seed evidence it does not hold at the opening: the finding entry's amount_usd is 0.00.
    Resolving action: the assessment action, owner agent.
  edge 2: rentals_ext_counter_settlement <- rentals_ext_late_handin_fee.
    kind value_input, gate shop_fees_raised, form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "The amount the guest is asked to hand over is fixed only after the
    account carries the shop fee owed for the days the kit stayed out beyond the date written on the
    agreement."
    Four-point test: (1) "only after"; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — a shop fee entry
    on the account — with no action named; (3) no code names; (4) the scope is exactly the fee owed
    for days beyond the date on the agreement, neither wider nor narrower. Exactly one write of this
    difficulty books that entry: the late hand-in fee policy's own action. Derivation: the sentence
    says the counter figure waits on that fee standing on the account; the records show a hand-in
    date later than the due date and no entry of the fee family at all; the late hand-in fee policy's
    rule says what such a fee is and how it is worked out; therefore that fee must be raised first.
    Seed evidence: the account's thirteen entries are one block load, six dates the kit was out,
    three rate-family charges, one security hold, one payment and one finding — none of the fee
    family.
    Resolving action: the late hand-in fee action, owner agent.
  edge 3: rentals_ext_security_hold_settlement <- rentals_ext_counter_settlement.
    kind value_input, gate money_collected, form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "What goes back to the guest is worked out only after the money collected
    against the agreement stands against the charges raised on it."
    Four-point test: (1) "only after"; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — money collected
    standing against the charges raised — naming no performer; (3) no code names; (4) hard
    requirement, scope exactly the charges raised on this agreement. Exactly one write of this
    difficulty books money collected: the counter settlement action. Derivation: the sentence says
    the release waits on money collected standing against the charges; the records show one payment
    of 375.50 answering to the hire rate entry alone and 65.00 still outstanding before this
    conversation adds anything; the counter settlement policy's rule says what the guest is asked to
    hand over and that it is handed over at the counter; therefore the settlement must happen first.
    Seed evidence: the single payment entry's amount_usd 375.50 and its related_event_id pointing at
    the hire rate entry, and the agreement's rental_balance_usd of 65.00.
    Resolving action: the counter settlement action, owner USER — the guest hands money over herself,
    the agent unlocks the action and passes it to her at its place in the order.
  topological order: assessment, late hand-in fee, counter settlement, release. The first two are
  parallel; order_uniqueness in the task file gives the replayed proof that they commute.
  value_input edges: 3, against the floor of max(3-1, 1) = 2.
  Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skipping the assessment moves the counter figure from
  120.19 to 109.19; skipping the fee moves it from 120.19 to 0.00; skipping the settlement moves the
  release from 628.00 to 478.51.
  No prerequisite rests on anything that has to happen outside this conversation: the finding is
  already on the record, the fee is a book entry, the payment is taken from a card the guest has in
  her hand, and the release is a book entry. No status write here stands in for a real-world event.

FACTOR CARD (the Step 5 sensitivity run is quoted per factor in each computation's factor_trace;
figures repeated here for the reviewer).

    use_intensity_share -> 16 percent (baseline 10) -> 38.00; delivered_kit_setaside -> 20 percent

    school_delivery_share (lessons) -> 70 percent (baseline the whole) -> 87.00; waiver_cover_share

  rentals_ext_late_handin_fee (5 factors, 3 parameter + 2 method): overdue_stretch_anchor (method)
    -> 292.25; resident_relief_days (lodging) -> 365.31; daily_figure_basis (method) -> 134.64;
    household_standing_share (passes, multi-source) -> 398.52; kit_exposure_uplift -> 182.66. Whole

  rentals_ext_counter_settlement (4 factors, 3 parameter + 1 method): counter_settlement_order
    (method, lodging) -> 185.19; resort_credit_offset (passes) -> 205.19;
    service_goodwill_allowance -> 145.19; assessment_left_to_hold -> 170.19. Whole baseline 345.19
    against gold 120.19.
  rentals_ext_security_hold_settlement (5 factors, 4 parameter + 1 method): folio_transfer_scope
    (lodging, multi-source) -> 478.00; protection_cover_offset (insure) -> 578.00;
    open_assessment_margin -> 645.00; household_standing_allowance (passes, multi-source) -> 568.00;
    retained_amount_method (method) -> 628.75. Whole baseline 425.00 against gold 628.00.
  Multi-source factors of the task: household_standing_share, folio_transfer_scope,
  household_standing_allowance, delivered_kit_setaside, school_delivery_share,
  model_change_inspection_setaside, service_goodwill_allowance. Cross-difficulty factors:
  school_delivery_share (lessons), delivered_kit_setaside (lodging), resident_relief_days (lodging),
  household_standing_share (passes), counter_settlement_order (lodging), resort_credit_offset
  (passes), folio_transfer_scope (lodging), protection_cover_offset (insure),
  household_standing_allowance (passes). No factor's tier is read off a stamp: every one rests on
  counted or summed ledger rows, a date span, or another product's holding and ledger.
  Near misses planted on purpose: the two out-of-window lift scans from the previous season; the
  school tuition entry that is not a session delivered; the two dates the kit was out on the serial
  the rider held before the change of model; the waiver charged for four dates against six dates out.
  Inherited base boundaries that this task does not touch: the fitting range, the term bounds, the
  hold placement state, the closure condition. The only base clauses superseded are declared in the
  six overwrite entries — the waiver excess sentence, the flat per-day late fee sentence, the two
  replacement-route sentences of the late return policy, and the hold release sentence of the deposit
  and damage policy — each naming the base sentence it replaces and the extended sentence that takes
  its place.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS.
  customers: the household the call is about; remove it and nothing can be located or verified.
  rentals_holdings: the agreement every computation reads; it carries the dates the stretch and the
    settlement gap are measured on, the package that supplies every tier parameter, the change count,
    the waiver flag, the hold and the outstanding figure.
  rentals_ledger block load + six dates out: the day history. Remove the dates and the use-intensity
    share, the inspection set-aside, the waiver cover share and the goodwill allowance all fall to
    other tiers.
  rentals_ledger rate, waiver and delivery charges: what the agreement has been charged. Remove the
    delivery charge and the delivered set-aside falls to nothing; remove the waiver entry and the
    cover share falls to the bare tier; remove either and what the agreement still owes changes.
  rentals_ledger security hold: the exposure uplift, the deferral against the hold, the retained
    amount method's fall-back and the whole release quantity rest on it.
  rentals_ledger payment: what has already been collected, and the payment count the retained amount
    method reads.
  rentals_ledger finding: the object the assessment is written onto and the gate edge 1 falsifies.
  rentals_requests extension: the anchor the overdue stretch is counted from and the condition the
    goodwill allowance rests on.
  passes_holdings + passes_ledger: the standing share, the credit offset and the standing allowance.
  lodging_holdings: the resident relief, the delivered set-aside, the counter settlement order and
    the folio transfer.
  lessons_holdings + lessons_ledger: the school delivery share.
  insure_holdings: the protection cover offset.
  Automatic-clause check: the base charter's automatic clauses on this category are the reservation
  hold period running out into an uncollected reservation, the grace period running out into an
  overdue flag, and closure once nothing is left to collect. None is lit here: the kit was collected,
  so no uncollected reservation can arise; the agreement already stands returned rather than out, so
  no overdue flag is owed; and the agreement still owes money at the end of this conversation, so
  closure is not owed either and nothing in the task set is left hanging. No cache field is used as a
  trap in this task: the agreement's damage_deposit_usd and rental_balance_usd both agree exactly
  with the ledger sums at the opening.

PERSONA DESIGN. Marta Sandoval-Reyes is written brisk and unfussy — she states the hold in her first
breath and then waits, which keeps the surface goal narrow and gives the agent nothing to lean on.
What she volunteers is only the hold, the shop, and that she took the skis back on the Saturday;
every one of those is carried by a seeded row. Her identity details come out one layer at a time and
only on request, which is why the verification step has exactly two matching credentials rather than
six. Her memory of the week — the collection date, the request to keep the kit a day longer that
nobody answered, the studio and the drive home on the second — is natural circumstance, each item
independently true of the seed, and it is the sort of thing a guest actually remembers; it also gives
a careless agent the chance to take her word for a date the record settles. She explicitly cannot
confirm the hand-in date from memory and says she would have to check her photographs, so the branch
where the agent asks has a definite answer rather than an improvised one. Her passive reactions are
woven into the narration rather than scripted as conditions: she agrees to the agent acting on the
shop's side once told something has to be settled first, and she pays with her own card once told
money is outstanding and asked to clear it. She never offers a figure and never disputes one, so she
cannot pull a wrong agent back onto the path, and she closes on hearing that the hold has been dealt
with and how much is going back.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Turn by turn: she gives a name and a mobile, which locate the
account; she gives a date of birth, which completes verification; the agent reads the agreement, the
rental account, the shop requests, the pass and its entries, the lodging reservation, the school
booking and its entries, and the protection plan — all through share tools, all synchronous. The
technician's finding is already on the record, so nothing waits on a workshop. The fee and the
assessment are book entries. The payment is taken from a card the guest is holding, at the agent's
hand-over, and her own line covers it. The release is a book entry. Every must-ask question has an
answer in the persona, including the two she cannot answer, and the whole tree runs under one
frozen_time with no waiting, no clearing and no future date. Nothing here is a status registration
standing in for a real-world event: no tool writes "completed" for anything that has not happened.

WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT.
  Counting the overdue stretch from the date on the agreement (six days) instead of from the date the
  guest asked to keep the kit to (five) — the rule's anchor tiers settle it, and the request is on the
  record.
  Forgetting the lodging departure relief and charging five days instead of three.
  Taking the package's flat daily late fee of 68.00 instead of the marked-up multi-day rate, because
  the advance booking lead and the multi-day threshold are both met.
  Counting all thirteen pass entries, or the two previous-season scans, as scans in the window.
  Reading the waiver as covering the whole hire: the entry's quantity is 4 against six dates out.
  Counting six dates the kit was out toward the inspection set-aside instead of the four on the
  serial the agreement now shows.
  Counting the school tuition entry as a session delivered.
  Paying the whole outstanding balance at the counter instead of only the fees and the assessment,
  because the household holds lodging.
  Releasing the whole hold, or releasing it before the guest has settled — the prerequisite sentence
  and the retained amount method both bite, and releasing first gives a terminal hash of a release of
  0.00 rather than 628.00.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify. Read the agreement, the rental account, the shop requests, the
pass, the pass entries, the lodging reservation, the school booking, the school entries and the
protection plan. Work out the assessment on the technician's finding: 1650.00 at 16 percent = 264.00;
less 20 percent delivered set-aside = 211.20; less 15 percent inspection set-aside = 179.52; at 70
percent school share = 125.66; at 60 percent partial cover = 75.40; at 80 percent carried up = 61.00.
Write it onto the finding. Work out the late hand-in fee: stretch 2027-02-02 to 2027-02-06 = 5 days;
less 2 days of resident relief = 3; daily figure 82.00 x 1.35 = 110.70; x 55 percent standing share;
x 1.20 exposure uplift; 3 x 110.70 x 0.55 x 1.20 = 219.186 -> 219.19. Raise it. Work out the counter
figure: fees 219.19 + assessment 61.00 = 280.19; less credit 85.00, goodwill 25.00 and 50.00 left
against the hold = 120.19. Unlock the counter action and hand it to the guest, who pays. Work out the
release: charges 720.69 less collected 495.69 = 225.00; less folio transfer 120.00 and plan cover
40.00 = 65.00; x 1.25 = 81.25; less standing allowance 60.00 = 21.25; carried up = 22.00; 650.00 -
22.00 = 628.00, recorded as partially forfeited.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The four computations were evaluated by the gate's own machinery on the
handling-time world (initial_state plus every earlier gold write), problem by problem in topological
order, and the per-factor baseline substitutions and the whole-baseline substitution were replayed on
the same worlds. Command and output:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/equipment_rental_desk --task 0
  rentals_ext_damage_assessment = 61.0 ; rentals_ext_late_handin_fee = 219.19 ;
  rentals_ext_counter_settlement = 120.19 ; rentals_ext_security_hold_settlement = 628.0
  per-factor baselines: 38.00 / 76.00 / 71.00 / 87.00 / 21.00 / 75.40 ; 292.25 / 365.31 / 134.64 /
  398.52 / 182.66 ; 185.19 / 205.19 / 145.19 / 170.19 ; 478.00 / 578.00 / 645.00 / 568.00 / 628.75
  whole baselines: 33.00 / 408.00 / 345.19 / 425.00, each different from its gold.
Every figure above is equal to the corresponding computations entry and to the gold argument at its
step. A first run of the assessment and the release produced 60.00 and 629.00 because the
carry-up-to-the-whole-dollar step had been written with a truncating conversion, which floors rather
than carries up; symptom: the machine figure disagreed with the hand calculation by one dollar; root
cause: int() truncates toward zero; change: both expressions now use floor division on the negated
value; re-run: 61.00 and 628.00, matching the hand calculation, and the counter figure moved with
them from 119.19 to 120.19. The tracing, the factor traces, the edge_load_bearing entries and this
worklog were all updated in the same pass.

FORWARD AND REVERSE SWEEP. Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice carries a
verbatim quotation of the rule sentence it implements in compute_basis — the aggregation bindings,
the cross-category reads, every ladder, every cap and every rounding. Reverse: reading each rule
through, the sentences carrying a quantity, a window, a filter, a branch, an order or a rounding are
all claimed. The windows ("in the four months before", "in the eight months before") correspond to
within_months on the matching aggregate; the filters ("of the assessment family", "waiver charged for
dates") correspond to the event_type and charge_category filters; the branch words ("where ...
instead") correspond to ternaries; the caps ("up to the deferral cap", "capped at the folio transfer
cap") correspond to MN; the rounding words correspond to RND, to the halving and taking down to the
whole dollar below, and to the carrying up to the whole dollar above. Each rule states its acting
base, its order and the moment of its rounding in plain prose: the assessment's set-asides act each
on the amount left after the step before it and are rounded at each of those steps; the late fee's
share and uplift act on the daily figure itself rather than on one another's results and only the fee
is rounded; the counter settlement's three deductions each act on the figure the counter step arrived
at and none acts on another's result; the release's folio transfer and plan cover are both taken off
before the multiple is applied and the allowance after it.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. Every one of the four calls carries its business effect, its
request binding with an intent source and a discriminator, its stage provenance and its base
preconditions. The two policy_scope entries (the assessment and the counter payment) are used only
where the governing base policy has no gate whose applies_to reaches the realized subject; the two
gated writes (the fee and the release) bind rentals_holdings.rental_id, the blueprint's own
correlation key, to the call's rental_id, and the time gate deep-copies the base temporal basis and
gives a just-before and an at-boundary case. Stage provenance is honest: the technician's finding
pre-exists the call and cites its own seeded row; the fee is performed by its own tool; the counter
payment and the release are established by prior steps and cite them.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and
this worklog masked, and working only from the policy prose that the knowledge base will carry, the
four tool schemas, the rows the share tools return and the caller's own lines: the caller asks about
the hold; the release rule says what goes back is the hold standing less what is kept back and that
it is worked out only after the money collected stands against the charges raised; the account shows
one payment answering to the hire rate alone and 65.00 outstanding, so that state does not hold; the
settlement rule says what the guest is asked to hand over and states that it waits on findings
carrying amounts and on the fee for days beyond the date on the agreement; the account shows a
finding at nil and no fee entry, so both of those must come first; the assessment rule and the late
fee rule each yield one number on the records as they stand. Working the four numbers through gives
61.00, 219.19, 120.19 and 628.00 and the order assessment, fee, settlement, release — the same
conclusion, the same objects, the same parameters and the same order as gold, with no second reading
available, since every tier condition is settled by a record rather than by judgement.

REVISION RECORD (second). Symptom: the compute gate reported that the security hold policy's
household_standing_allowance factor "reads 'passes' event history but the world seeds no matching
rows for this customer". Root cause: the tier had been written to count instalments the payment
method refused, an entry family this household's pass account correctly carries none of, so the
cross-difficulty evidence the gate insists on could not exist without seeding a refusal the rest of
the world contradicts (the pass is paid in full). Change: the tier now reads the pass record's own
instalment balance through a cross-category field read rather than an event count, which is the same
business question — whether the collective still has money to collect from this household — asked of
the record that actually answers it. Re-run: COMPUTE OK. The figures did not move, because the pass
shows nothing still to be collected and the clean tier still applies: 61.00, 219.19, 120.19, 628.00.
Propagated in the same pass to the rule, the compute bindings, compute_basis, the factor's ladder and
bindings, the policy's cross_category note and inputs, the factor_trace and factor_sensitivity of the
security hold computation, the read node necessities for the pass and the pass account, and this
worklog.

Marta Sandoval-Reyes is forty-seven, a structural engineer in Salt Lake City who has skied Silverpine Basin since she was a student and now holds a season pass there. She is brisk and good-humoured, the sort of caller who states the thing in the first breath and then waits to be told. The thing, this morning, is a hold: a six hundred and fifty dollar hold from the demo skis she hired at Silverpine is still sitting against her card, she noticed it going through the statement over breakfast, and she would like somebody to deal with it. She and her sister had a slopeside studio for that week and she drove home on the second of February.
